targets.title: Machine learning to analyze single-case graphs: A comparison to visual inspection.
targets.evidence_quote: Therefore, the purpose of our study was to replicate and extend Lanovaz and Hranchuk by (a) comparing proportions of false positives produced by the models in nonsimulated data comprised of AB graphs with different phase lengths and (b) identifying graph characteristics that are likely to lead the models to produce errors.
targets.outcome_quote: Reducing errors, even to a small degree, may lead to more frequent appropriate decisions, which may be worthwhile for the small proportion of human participants and clients for whom a better decision was rendered. Taken together, these results underline the promising nature of the support vector classifier for analyzing single-case data and would merit further attention in future research. Interestingly, the stochastic gradient descent classifier produced considerably more Type I errors than the conservative dual-criteria method, which is contrary to the pattern observed by Lanovaz and Hranchuk (2021).
targets.outcome_reasoning: The support vector classifier advantage agrees with the original, but the authors explicitly contrast the stochastic gradient descent result with the original: it produced considerably more Type I errors than the conservative dual-criteria method, contrary to the original pattern. These are two comparisons rather than an overall confirming verdict.

reasoning: Tests the 2021 models on a different, nonsimulated sample. The 2017 paper supplies the dataset and comparison values; its finding is not itself the target. Taylor and Lanovaz (2022) is background, not the target.
